meta.notes: Most problem evidence is vendor marketing (STRATAFOLIO, Prophia, PredictAP, Springbord); error-rate statistics (30-40%) are secondary citations whose primary studies could not be located. BiggerPockets threads, Yardi.com, jmco.com (Yardi consultant), TrustRadius/Capterra/Software Advice, Dice and several job boards were blocked by robots.txt or 403, so the forum voice and Yardi-consultant cost claims are missing. No public evidence found for the 50-80 consultant hours / $15k-$50k Yardi setup claim or for tenant bills 50-100% above estimates. Prospects use the primary ICP (large commercial PM firm) plus mid-market operators; no contacts recorded by instruction; technology fit unknown for all companies.

summary.statement: CAM reconciliation is done inside PM/accounting platforms (Yardi Breeze/Voyager, AppFolio, Re-Leased, Rent Manager, DoorLoop), many of which claim to handle caps, base years and gross-ups.
Spreadsheets remain common where the system lacks CAM support or for complex leases, and IREM teaches Excel CAM templates.
In-house property accountants do the work as a core annual duty, and some firms outsource it to service providers.
No source described how lease terms are extracted in mid-market firms beyond manual abstraction and abstraction vendors.
Vendors claim 20+ hours per property per year manually, and that the cycle consumes most of Q1 for retail teams; these are marketing figures.
Senior property accountants who own CAM reconciliations are paid about $90-95k a year in one posting.
Existing CAM software is cheap: Yardi Breeze commercial at $2/unit/month and STRATAFOLIO from $190/month, which constrains pricing.
No public evidence found for the claimed 50-80 consultant hours ($15k-$50k) to set up Yardi recoveries.
Property management teams often make proptech decisions independently (IREM survey via NAR).
No source identified who approves or pays for a CAM sidecar specifically (controller vs. VP property management vs. CFO).
Secondary sources cite CAM reconciliation error rates of 30-40%, but the primary studies could not be located.
A tenant audit of one year of CAM takes about two months, and disputes can delay or withhold payments.
One law-firm source suggests delayed billing is infrequent at large institutional landlords.
No source quantified how often disputes actually delay settlement of statements.

Tenant auditors request the full GL extract for the CAM pool, invoice backup (commonly above $5,000), service contracts, and management-fee and gross-up worksheets, usually within about 30 days of the request.
Backup today often arrives as 50-500 page mixed PDFs, and statements that lack detail trigger audits.

Alternatives include AI lease-abstraction tools (Prophia), CAM add-ons (STRATAFOLIO), PM suites (Re-Leased, DoorLoop, Rent Manager, AppFolio, Yardi), outsourced CAM services (Springbord, OHI, Withum) and Excel templates.
A comparison guide argues Yardi users should use Yardi's module rather than a second system.

Is $50-100 per property per month viable when STRATAFOLIO and Yardi Breeze price CAM-capable software far lower per unit?

current_solutions.statement: Most operators reconcile CAM inside their PM/accounting system (Yardi, AppFolio, Re-Leased, Rent Manager, DoorLoop), which vendors market as automated.
Spreadsheets are the fallback for unsupported systems and complex leases, and IREM trains managers to build Excel CAM templates.
Property accountants own CAM reconciliations and tenant audit support as a salaried annual duty.
Firms also outsource CAM reconciliation to service providers such as Springbord, OHI and Withum.
